task: Write and commit `docs/changes/W2-50-CIT-E.md`, the change-execution record (CAP-33) for DAEO-kl5e (W2-50), checked against the approved CIT-P and the owner's answers (DEC-743).
status: DONE. The CIT-E is committed as `b7981b0f` with `status: APPLIED`, and its frontmatter is valid against the schema.
work_completed: I read the ticket, the CIT-P with DEC-743, the branch log, the implementation diff `91200c82`, the code at HEAD (`runs.py`, `decide.py`, `launcher.py`, `secrets/__init__.py`), the acceptance README, S2-CIT-E and the schema. I wrote the CIT-E in five parts: (1) what was applied, with commits `a5ef3c69`, `887c288c` and `91200c82`; (2) each change 3(a) to 3(d) file by file, with 11 numbered differences; (3) the verification and the cases not run; (4) the size against the estimate; (5) what stays open. I changed no code and no test.
files_changed: docs/changes/W2-50-CIT-E.md
evidence: Commit `b7981b0f` "W2-50 (DAEO-kl5e): the change-execution record (CIT-E)", trailers `Task: DAEO-kl5e`, `Role: engineer`, `Implements: DEC-728`, `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. `git show --stat HEAD` shows 1 file, 243 insertions; `git status --short` is empty afterwards. The hooks folder holds only `*.sample` files. Checks at start: `GOV_ROLE=engineer`, `GOV_TICKET=DAEO-kl5e`, top level `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-50`, branch `w2/W2-50`. The `gov.__file__` line: `PYTHONPATH=/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-50/src python3 -c "import gov; print(gov.__file__)"` printed `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-50/src/gov/__init__.py`. Schema check: I validated the frontmatter with jsonschema 4.10.3 (Draft 2020-12) against `change-execution-record.schema.json`, resolving `common.schema.json`. Result: valid. S2-CIT-E, used as a control, is also valid. Negative controls were all rejected: a wrong `state_class`, a wrong `type`, a bad `id`, and a missing `status`. Size from `git show --numstat 91200c82`: code 100 added and 7 removed (decide 17/2, runs 54/0, launcher 13/1, secrets 16/4); builder tests 165/0; total 265/7.
tests: None run by me. The CIT-E records the lead's runs at `91200c82`: W2-50 154 passed; `tests/unit` 2113 passed, 1 skipped; W1-01 to W1-50 green except W1-42's two known reds (DEC-713, DEC-714); W1-46 and W1-50 run with `-m "not local_only"`, leaving 38 live-launch cases not run; `gov rebuild --json` ok. `validate_s1.py` was not run (DEC-738 item 2).
discoveries: These are the 11 differences recorded in the CIT-E. (1) A root that is itself a symbolic link gives no own folder. (2) A folder name that is empty, `.` or `..`, or that holds `/` or a NUL, gives no folder. (3) The guard's ticket loader also finds a ticket by its `wbs_id`; this was already true before the change, and R3 still holds. (4) The ticket's role need not be the session's role: any of the six roles gets the folder (R4 as written). (5) An `rmdir` argument the guard cannot resolve is dropped, not refused, so `rmdir "$VAR"` where the variable holds the root is allowed. This follows the root-only scope. (6) A refusal reason under the root is the guard's generic one, which names the target. (7) When the launcher cannot name or make the own folder, or finds a link or non-folder at its path, it starts the session with the temp folder only. It does not refuse and prints nothing; the CIT-P does not cover this case. (8) The launcher makes the folder before the temp folder and the signal handlers, so a launch interrupted early still leaves the folder on disk. (9) `secrets-indexing.yaml` did not change. The check's command stays `python3 -m gov.secrets` and the whole rule is in `src/gov/secrets/__init__.py`, under §6.1 (i). So W2-06 finds the yaml as it was. (10) A clone adopted under the root runs its own check over its own `.gov-runtime/`: the runtime folder's own paths are followed before the root rule applies. No test holds this. (11) `gov.secrets` now imports `gov.guard.runs`. How the answers were built: R7 judges `rmdir` only for a target equal to the root. R8 uses real-path resolution plus a rule that refuses an existing file with more than one hard link, with DEC-334's rule for making a link. §6.4 gives the folder only while the ticket is `in_progress`. §6.5 leaves `ticket-lead` out of the roles that get a folder.
risks: Difference 5 means `rmdir` of a variable that holds the root is not refused. Difference 7 means a launched worker may silently have no own folder. Difference 10 has no test, so a later change to the walk could make a clone's own check always green without any test failing. The 38 live launch cases have not run against this change.
lessons: The CIT-P named the yaml for 3(d), but §6.1 (i) moved the whole rule into the module. Read the code against the proposal's section headings, not only its text. No test runs the secrets check from a repository that lies under the root.
proposed_decisions: One package, on difference 7: what should a launch do when the own folder cannot be named or made? Options: (a) keep the current behaviour (start without the folder, silently); (b) start, but print one line saying the session has no own folder; (c) refuse the launch. I recommend (b), placed in W2-21's launcher work. Confidence medium.
unresolved: W2-H055 (`git clone` destinations, W2-09); W2-M359 (Write and Edit in a launched session, W2-21); W2-L342 (CAP-58's text, Wave 3); the 38 live `local_only` cases and the real `~/gov-os-runs/`; `rmdir` under the root and of an unresolvable argument (W2-09); difference 7 (W2-21 or owner); difference 10 has no test (W2-14, W2-15a or W2-06).
recommended_next_action: Start the fresh FULL reviewer probe of `91200c82` against the CIT-E, and put the difference-7 package to the owner or W2-21.
